primitives.name: Approval-Gated State Transition Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: Start in docs or a sandbox and only move into app code after explicit approval.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: \mathcal{S}: state space (dimensionless); \alpha: approval predicate (Boolean, dimensionless); \mathcal{T}: transition operator (dimensionless)
primitives.assumptions: Approval is binary and exogenous; no partial transitions; sandbox and docs states are observationally equivalent pre-approval.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Approval predicate becomes stochastic or multi-valued; sandbox leaks into production via side channels.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSE situational reasoning: state vector s_t \in \mathcal{S} evolves via s_{t+1} = \mathcal{T}_{\alpha_t}(s_t) where \alpha_t is the approval gate; telemetry is transition latency and gate-pass rate.
layer2.telemetry: Mean dwell time in docs/sandbox; approval pass/fail ratio; sandbox-to-app promotion rate.

primitives.name: Legal-Security-Repo Boundary Constraint Manifold
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Legal / License Boundary Allowed: study docs, use APIs, self-host in an isolated lab, and write original GSE integration code.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: \mathcal{B}: feasible set (dimensionless); \text{license}(x): license category (categorical); \text{secrets}(x): secret presence (Boolean); \text{allowed paths}: filesystem path predicate (Boolean)
primitives.assumptions: Boundaries are static during card execution; license categories are mutually exclusive; secret detection is perfect.
primitives.breakdown_regime: License reclassification mid-execution; secret scanning false negatives; path traversal via symlinks.

layer2.mapping: GSI conformal inference: boundary predicates define the calibration set; any proposed integration x must satisfy x \in \mathcal{B} with coverage guarantee 1-\alpha. GSE maps \mathcal{B} to CI/CD gate predicates.
layer2.telemetry: Boundary violation count per card; false-positive rate of secret scanner; license classification accuracy.

primitives.name: OSS Leverage to Bounded Workflow Conversion Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Why It Matters This improves decision quality, revenue, speed, support, retention, trust, or cost savings by converting open-source leverage into a bounded GSE workflow.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: \mathcal{L}_{\text{OSS}}: OSS artifact space (dimensionless); \mathcal{B}: boundary manifold (dimensionless); \mathcal{W}_{\text{GSE}}: workflow space (dimensionless); \mathcal{K}: conversion kernel (dimensionless)
primitives.assumptions: OSS leverage is quantifiable as artifact set; conversion is deterministic given boundaries; acceptance criteria are decidable.
primitives.breakdown_regime: OSS artifact space expands beyond boundary containment; acceptance criteria become undecidable; kernel output violates boundary.

layer2.mapping: GSI Bayesian: \mathcal{L}_{\text{OSS}} provides prior evidence; \mathcal{B} defines likelihood support; \mathcal{W}_{\text{GSE}} is posterior mode. GSE: kernel implements the D. Support/Customer Success workflow transformation.
layer2.telemetry: Decision quality delta; workflow cycle time reduction; SaaS cost displacement (post-pricing refresh).

primitives.name: Documented Rollback Involution
primitives.verbatim_quote: Avoid `.env*`, Stripe/billing code, launch gates, production deploy config, and unrelated app files.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: \mathcal{R}: rollback operator (dimensionless); \mathcal{S}: state space; s_0: pre-card baseline state; \mathcal{S}_{\text{card}}: card-affected subspace
primitives.assumptions: Card changes are confined to docs/spec files or isolated branch; baseline state s_0 is recoverable; no production side effects.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Card changes leak into production via untracked dependencies; baseline state corrupted; rollback documentation outdated.

layer2.mapping: GSE state-transition: \mathcal{R} is the inverse transition for the docs-first subspace; telemetry is rollback invocation frequency and time-to-restore. GSI: conformal guarantee that production state remains in pre-card prediction set.
layer2.telemetry: Rollback invocation rate; mean time to restore baseline; production state divergence metric.

reasoning_traces.think:
The BUILD-044 card defines a controlled conversion of OSS artifacts (Chatwoot, AnythingLLM) into a GSE workflow via a gated state-transition system. The approval gate \alpha creates a discontinuous transition manifold: states in docs/sandbox are topologically separated from app-code states until \alpha=1. The boundary manifold \mathcal{B} is the intersection of three constraint submanifolds (legal, security, repo), each defined by predicate logic over artifact properties. The conversion kernel \mathcal{K} maps the product space \mathcal{L}_{\text{OSS}} \times \mathcal{B} to workflow space \mathcal{W}_{\text{GSE}}, effectively a projection onto the feasible subspace. The rollback involution \mathcal{R} provides a left-inverse for the card's action on the docs/spec subspace, guaranteeing \mathcal{R} \circ \mathcal{T}_{\alpha} = \text{id} on \mathcal{S}_{\text{card}} when \alpha=0. Failure modes: (1) \alpha becomes stochastic due to ambiguous approval criteria; (2) \mathcal{B} develops holes via license reclassification or secret-scanner false negatives; (3) \mathcal{K} output escapes \mathcal{B} via supply-chain leakage; (4) \mathcal{R} fails because card changes couple to production through untracked dependencies. The docs-first strategy ensures \mathcal{S}_{\text{card}} \cap \mathcal{S}_{\text{prod}} = \emptyset initially, making \mathcal{R} trivial (file deletion).
